description.en: Measure the power consumed by a three-phase resistive load using the two-wattmeter method for Star and Delta connections.
Read the connection sequence and procedure for the selected load configuration.
Choose the load configuration with the MCB off. When converting Star to Delta, keep the supply and meter wires. Replace (17–19), (19–21) with (16–19), (18–21), (17–20).
Get spoken guidance and highlighted terminals for the next required connection. Click again to stop.
Verify the selected circuit. Correct any Invalid Connections before proceeding after Right Connections.
Make the selected load connections automatically, then click CHECK.
After verification, switch on the MCB to energize the three-phase load. Switch it off before editing wires or changing configuration. Terminals: 1, 2, 3.
Measure line voltage VL between two phases. Terminals: 4, 5. The experiment uses 408 V.
Measure line current IL. Terminals: 6, 7. Star reads 0.5 A and Delta reads 1.2 A.
The first wattmeter measures one part of the total three-phase power. Terminals: 8, 9, 10, 11.
The second wattmeter completes the two-wattmeter measurement. Terminals: 12, 13, 14, 15. Total measured power is W1 + W2.
The three load branches have left terminals 16, 18, 20 and right terminals 17, 19, 21. Lamps are off until the verified MCB is on. Star glows dimly; Delta glows brightly.
Record VL, IL, W1, W2 and their total. Record one reading for each configuration.
Compare the Star and Delta readings. Star total power is 370 W; Delta total power is 840 W.
For the resistive load, cosφ = 1 and theoretical power P = √3 × VL × IL. Compare W1 + W2 with P to calculate percentage error.
After adding both readings, plot the power comparison and measurement errors.
After plotting, generate the experiment report with observations, calculations, graph and result.
Clear connections and readings and return to the initial Star setup.
Print the simulation using the browser print dialog.
